subject: VortexX: request for temporary SLA concession due to model p95 regression
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha@vortexx.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Kapoor <ravi.kapoor@vortexx.com>, VortexX Payments Eng Team <payments@vortexx.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike — payments API (p95 > 1s)

Mateo,

We're seeing an abrupt increase in p95 on the payments inference path starting at ~08:45 PDT after the variant rollout to vx-llm-3b-q4. Baseline p95 was ~210ms; current p95 is ~1.1s and some user requests time out. This is impacting checkout conversion.

Attached is a snapshot from our telemetry (vz-perf-snapshot-20280719.csv) and a short timeline. Can Redwood confirm whether a model variant change or infra config was pushed on your side? If this is a model regression, we need a temporary SLA concession and a rollback plan while we coordinate mitigations.

We're available for a call in the next 30 minutes — Ravi and I will be on standby.

Thanks,
Asha Menon
Senior Platform Engineer, VortexX Payments
asha@vortexx.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

Attachment: vz-perf-snapshot-20280719.csv (CSV, 85KB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Menon <asha@vortexx.com>, Ravi Kapoor <ravi.kapoor@vortexx.com>, VortexX Payments Eng Team <payments@vortexx.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — payments API (p95 > 1s)

Team — looping you in. Asha reports p95 jumping to ~1.1s after the vx-llm-3b-q4 rollout. I pulled internal logs for VX-3245 and there's a variant promotion at 08:40 PDT that moved ~35% traffic to the q4 quantized variant.

Quick summary of ask from VortexX: temporary SLA concession (they're seeing user-facing timeouts) and authorization to trigger a fallback to the previous variant while we investigate. They want an explicit time window and rollback authority.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Approve a temporary SLA carveout for up to 72 hours while we revert/mitigate (if approved by risk/compliance).
- Ops: push traffic back to vx-llm-3b-v1 (stable) and hold new variant traffic at 0% for the next 2 hours.
- Engineering: run a perf delta (quantized q4 vs v1) and deliver p95 breakdowns (attach redwood-ma-p95-comparison-07-19.png).

Can we get a quick sign-off? Asha is asking for a written concession to share with procurement. I can coordinate the rollback immediately once we have authorization.

— Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0124

Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — payments API (p95 > 1s)

Thanks for the rapid escalation, Mateo. I've reviewed the timeline and the preliminary perf artifacts. Given the customer impact (payment timeouts) and the rollout correlation, I'm authorizing a short-term SLA concession under the following constraints:

1) We authorize a maximum 72-hour SLA grace period starting at the time we revert traffic (documented start time required).
2) Engineering must push the fallback to vx-llm-3b-v1 within 30 minutes of sign-off and provide a post-fallback p95 report at T+30m and T+2h.
3) Customer must acknowledge the concession in writing (simple email confirmation is acceptable) so our legal team can record the temporary amendment.
4) Ops must create a change ticket and schedule a post-mortem within 48 hours; do not leave the variant pinned without approval from product.

I'll also require a short risk note in HubSpot and a one-page amendment to the SOW; I generated a draft DocuSign link for the amendment. Lease the HubSpot record: 78910.

DocuSign draft: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC-VMX-2028 (internal link — send to procurement after customer ack).

Once you confirm the rollback plan, I approve the 72-hour concession. Ben, can you coordinate the rollback and ensure we capture the metric artifacts for the post-mortem? Grace, please standby for customer comms.

-Kimberly
Head of Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: VortexX: temporary SLA concession confirmed and rollback schedule

Asha / Ravi — thanks for the quick collaboration. Per Kimberly's authorization, Redwood is granting a temporary SLA concession for VortexX (VX-3245) to address the p95 regression tied to vx-llm-3b-q4. Summary and next steps below: 

- Concession window: 72 hours starting at 16:00 PDT on 2028-07-19 (we recorded the rollback start at that time).
- Action taken: Ops rolled traffic back to vx-llm-3b-v1 at 16:00 PDT and held q4 at 0%.
- Observed post-fallback p95: 210–240ms at T+30m, stable. Full artifacts attached (redwood-ma-p95-comparison-07-19.png).
- Required from VortexX: please reply to this thread with a brief acknowledgment of the concession for our legal records (simple line confirming you accept the temporary window).
- Follow-ups: Engineering will run a 48-hour regression investigation and we will schedule a post-mortem with your team no later than 48 hours from now. Ben will lead the technical post-mortem.

I've attached the timeline we shared earlier (vortexx-timelines.pdf) and the telemetry snapshot. Once we have your written acknowledgment, we'll route the DocuSign amendment to procurement per Kimberly's note.

If you want us to keep the temporary concession shorter than 72 hours, tell us and we will update the start/end times accordingly.

Thanks again for the rapid escalation; we'll keep you posted.

— Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0124
